title: Quran
author: Unknown
current_text: In March 1985, Chandmal Chopra petitioned the Calcutta High Court to ban the Quran, alleging that it incited violence and promoted enmity among different sections; the High Court disallowed the petition on May 17, 1985. A district court in Novorossiysk ruled that a translation of the Quran by Elmir Kuliyev was extremist and should be included on the federal list of banned literature; the Krasnodar regional court overturned that ruling. Malaysia’s Home Ministry prohibited 10 translations of the Quran in Malay, English, Chinese and Korean; the ministry’s chief secretary, Alwi Ibrahim, said they had been printed without the original verses in Arabic.

sources.quote: Chandmal Chopra had filed a petition for a ban on the Quran in Calcutta High Court in March 1985 as it allegedly incites violence and promotes enmity among different sections. The petition was disallowed by the High Court on May 17, 1985.
sources.title: Explained: Quran case in Supreme Court, and the powers of judicial review | Explained News - The Indian Express

sources.quote: On December 17, the Krasnodar regional court overturned a September ruling by a district court in Novorossiysk that a translation of the Quran by Elmir Kuliyev was extremist and should be included on the federal list of banned literature. The Krasnodar judge remarked that the initial examination of the translation was made incorrectly by people lacking expertise.

The Home Ministry has gazetted a prohibition order on 22 publications, effective Sept 28 and Oct 3.
The ministry’s chief secretary, Alwi Ibrahim, said among the publications were 10 translations of the Quran in Malay, English, Chinese and Korean languages as they were printed without the original verses in Arabic.
sources.title: Home Minister gazettes prohibition order on 22 publications | Malaysiakini

ban_rows.note: In 1985, Chandmal Chopra filed a writ petition at the Calcutta High Court seeking to ban the Quran, claiming it incited religious disharmony. The petition was dismissed in May 1985 and a review petition was dismissed on 21 June 1985; the Union and West Bengal governments argued against it.
In 2013, a Russian court in Novorossiysk banned a translation of the Quran by Elmir Kuliyev under the country's 'extremism' laws. The ban was soon overturned.
